analysis.title: Nordic Alert: Nvidia leadership crisis, higher oil prices and yields, weighed on equities
key_insights: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on 12 November, after admitting earlier in the week to a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.
SEB says the Nvidia resignation, higher Brent oil prices and higher interest rates hurt risk appetite. US stocks fell (S&P 500 -0.4%, Nasdaq -0.4%), while European stocks rose (Euro Stoxx 50 +0.1%).
The euro weakened against the dollar and gold fell. Japanese stocks were opening higher and Chinese stocks lower.

Today's data: final October inflation for France, Spain and Poland, the second estimate of Q3 euro area GDP and employment, US October producer prices, Russian inflation and Turkey's September current account.
The only central bank rate decision today is Peru, where a 25 basis point hike is expected.
Central bank speakers today: the Fed's Mary Daly, Michelle Bowman and Susan Collins, and the ECB's Isabel Schnabel, Ante Žigman and Olaf Sleijpen.
Credit rating updates are expected for Bulgaria (S&P), Germany (Fitch) and Ukraine (Moody's).

Nordics: the krona weakened and the OMX30 ended unchanged. The Center Party leader has asked Moderate leader Ulf Kristersson and Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson for concrete government proposals by 5 p.m. today. The Riksbank's General Council meets at 1 p.m.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The report only lists it as the day's one central bank announcement and gives no market read.

risk_factors: Nvidia leadership uncertainty after the CEO's resignation
Higher Brent oil prices and higher interest rates weighing on risk appetite
Limited Starshield service for Ukraine's armed forces
geopolitical: President Trump said the U.S. does not need a deal with Iran and told Vice President J.D. Vance to focus on corruption in opposition-controlled electoral districts.
Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexico if its government does not stop a group of about 1,500 migrants walking toward the U.S. border.
Ukraine's President Zelenskyy said Starshield service has again been limited for Ukraine's armed forces, which makes its drone defense difficult.
